input.quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
input.rationale: On re-examination the refund limb of the remedy does not hold up, so I have moved this from compliant to deviation. Section 19.4 refunds "Fees paid for it", and "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as meaning only the "Implementation Fee", which § 1.6 fixes as the one-time USD 12,000 implementation charge in the first Order Form. Read through the definitions, the refund is therefore capped at implementation money and can never return the subscription fees we pay for Hosted Services or for Deliverables — the very amounts at risk if the full-term Hosted Services conformance warranty in § 19.2 is breached. The rule requires a real remedy of repair, replacement or refund; a refund that structurally excludes the principal consideration is not one, so the defect is substantive rather than cosmetic and sits in the remedy element the playbook treats as essential. The fix is minimal and surgical: key the refund to all amounts paid for the affected item, including prepaid subscription and other charges and expressly not limited to the Implementation Fee. The re-perform/repair/replace ladder, the reasonable-period trigger and the non-exclusivity carve-out for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims are all left untouched. I also stated the Deliverable warranty period as "ninety (90) days" in numerals in § 19.2. That is a clarity conform only, not a change of term: the period already ran ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance, and expressing it in digits removes any doubt that the 90-day floor is met while keeping the drafting consistent with the rest of the Agreement. Every other element of the rule remains satisfied and needs no edit: § 19.1 gives professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications, reinforced by § 3.1; § 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term, which meets or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark given "Services" is defined at § 1.8 to include the hosted software; § 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance, no malicious code, no mid-term functionality diminution and open-source protection for our source code; and § 19.5 confines the disclaimer to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies, so no disclaimer carve-out is needed. § 21.4 preserves the caps on failure of an exclusive remedy without recasting § 19.4 as a sole remedy, and § 6 supports the warranty trigger. The residual narrowing of the malicious-code warranty to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" remains customary and not worth negotiating capital at medium severity.

proposal.summary: Express the 90-day warranty period numerically and scope the warranty refund to all amounts paid for the non-conforming item, not just the narrowly defined "Fees".
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The warranty standards, duration and remedy ladder in Section 19 work for us, but "Fees" is defined in Section 1.5 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, so the refund limb of Section 19.4 would return implementation charges alone and never the subscription fees paid for non-conforming Hosted Services or Deliverables. We have keyed the refund to all amounts paid for the affected item and stated the ninety (90) day period in numerals for clarity; our playbook requires repair, replacement or a real refund remedy.
